## Overview

POST /api/owners is handled by `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner(...)`. The controller implements the OpenAPI-generated `OwnersApi` interface (which supplies the actual `@RequestMapping`, `@Valid`, and `@RequestBody` annotations). The request body type is `OwnerFieldsDto`. The flow is: Bean Validation on the DTO → MapStruct maps DTO→`Owner` (normalizing telephone) → two uniqueness checks in the controller → `ClinicServiceImpl.saveOwner` (generates customer code, saves) → JPA `@PrePersist` defaults the registration date → map entity→`OwnerDto` for the 201 response.

---

## 1. The controller method (POST /api/owners)

File: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`

Class annotations (lines 51-54): `@RestController`, `@CrossOrigin(...)`, `@RequestMapping("/api")`, implements `OwnersApi`.

The method, lines 99-116:
```java
99   @PreAuthorize("hasRole(@roles.OWNER_ADMIN)")
100  @Override
101  public ResponseEntity<OwnerDto> addOwner(OwnerFieldsDto ownerFieldsDto) {
102      HttpHeaders headers = new HttpHeaders();
103      Owner owner = ownerMapper.toOwner(ownerFieldsDto);
104      if (this.clinicService.existsOwnerByTelephone(owner.getTelephone())) {
105          return new ResponseEntity<>(HttpStatus.CONFLICT);
106      }
107      if (!Boolean.TRUE.equals(ownerFieldsDto.getSharesHousehold())
108          && this.clinicService.existsOwnerInHousehold(owner.getLastName(), owner.getAddress())) {
109          return new ResponseEntity<>(HttpStatus.CONFLICT);
110      }
111      this.clinicService.saveOwner(owner);
112      OwnerDto ownerDto = ownerMapper.toOwnerDto(owner);
113      headers.setLocation(UriComponentsBuilder.newInstance()
114          .path("/api/owners/{id}").buildAndExpand(owner.getId()).toUri());
115      return new ResponseEntity<>(ownerDto, headers, HttpStatus.CREATED);
116  }
```

Order of operations:
1. Security pre-check `@PreAuthorize` requires role OWNER_ADMIN.
2. Map DTO → `Owner` entity via `ownerMapper.toOwner(...)`.
3. Uniqueness check on telephone → 409 CONFLICT if a matching owner exists.
4. Household-uniqueness check (skipped when `sharesHousehold == true`) → 409 CONFLICT if an owner with same last name + normalized address exists.
5. `clinicService.saveOwner(owner)`.
6. Map saved `Owner` → `OwnerDto`.
7. Set `Location` header to `/api/owners/{id}`.
8. Return 201 CREATED with the DTO body.

### The `@Valid` / mapping annotations (generated interface)

File: `/home/daniel/sandbox/target/generated-sources/openapi/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/api/OwnersApi.java`
- Interface annotated `@Validated` (line 44).
- Lines 79-87: `@RequestMapping(method = POST, value = "/owners", produces/consumes application/json)` and the parameter `@Valid @RequestBody OwnerFieldsDto ownerFieldsDto`. So `@Valid` triggers Bean Validation on the DTO before the controller body runs. `PATH_ADD_OWNER = "/owners"` (line 52), combined with class-level `/api` → POST /api/owners.

Note: there is also a V2 owners controller (`OwnerRestControllerV2`) but it only implements `listOwnersPage` (GET); it does not handle POST.

## 2. Request DTO and all Bean Validation annotations

File: `/home/daniel/sandbox/target/generated-sources/openapi/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/dto/OwnerFieldsDto.java`

Field-level (lines 30-51) and getter-level constraints:

- `firstName` — `@NotBlank` (line 30); getter (line 77): `@NotNull @Pattern(regexp = "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$") @Size(min = 1, max = 30)`
- `lastName` — `@NotBlank` (line 33); getter (line 98): `@NotNull @Pattern(regexp = "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$") @Size(min = 1, max = 30)`
- `address` — `@NotBlank` (line 36); getter (line 119): `@NotNull @Size(min = 1, max = 255)`
- `city` — `@NotBlank` (line 39); getter (line 140): `@NotNull @Size(min = 1, max = 80)`
- `telephone` — `@NotBlank @org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation.Telephone` (line 42, custom validator); getter (line 161): `@NotNull @Size(min = 1, max = 20)`
- `email` — `@Email` (line 45, nullable); getter (line 182): `@Size(min = 1, max = 255) @Email`
- `registrationDate` — `@Nullable LocalDate`, `@DateTimeFormat(iso = DATE)` (line 48); getter `@Valid` (line 203). No presence constraint (optional).
- `sharesHousehold` — `Boolean`, defaults to `false` (line 51). No validation constraints; write-only flag, never persisted.

## 3. Service layer — `saveOwner` and the uniqueness checks

File: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/ClinicServiceImpl.java`

`existsOwnerByTelephone` (lines 246-250) — delegates to `ownerRepository.existsByTelephone(telephone)`. Note the controller passes `owner.getTelephone()`, which the mapper already normalized to E.164, so the comparison is against the normalized form.

`existsOwnerInHousehold` (lines 252-267):
```java
252  @Transactional(readOnly = true)
254  public boolean existsOwnerInHousehold(String lastName, String address) {
255      String normalizedAddress = normalizeForComparison(address);
256      return ownerRepository.findByLastNameIgnoreCase(lastName).stream()
257          .anyMatch(owner -> normalizeForComparison(owner.getAddress()).equals(normalizedAddress));
258  }
265  private static String normalizeForComparison(String value) {
266      return value == null ? "" : value.strip().replaceAll("\\s+", " ").toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
267  }
```
It finds owners with the same last name (case-insensitive) and checks whether any has an address equal after canonicalization (trim, collapse whitespace, lower-case).

`saveOwner` (lines 236-244):
```java
236  @Override
237  @Transactional
238  public void saveOwner(Owner owner) throws DataAccessException {
239      if (owner.isNew() && owner.getCustomerCode() == null) {
240          owner.setCustomerCode(customerCodeGenerator.generate(owner.getLastName(), ownerRepository.count() + 1));
241      }
242      ownerRepository.save(owner);
243  }
```
Side-effects in order:
1. If the owner is new (no id) and has no customer code, generate one: `customerCodeGenerator.generate(lastName, ownerRepository.count() + 1)` — a DB count query drives the sequence number.
2. Persist via `ownerRepository.save(owner)`.

`CustomerCodeGenerator.generate` — File `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/CustomerCodeGenerator.java`, lines 37-41: builds `<LAST3>-<NNNN>` — upper-cased first 3 letters of last name plus a 4-digit zero-padded sequence, e.g. `SMI-0007`.

Repository save — File `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/repository/jpa/JpaOwnerRepositoryImpl.java` (active under the `jpa` profile), lines 112-120: `em.persist(owner)` when id is null, otherwise `em.merge(owner)`. `existsByTelephone` (101-105) and `count` (108-110) are JPQL count queries; `findByLastNameIgnoreCase` (84-88) uses `LOWER(...) = LOWER(...)`. (A JDBC implementation also exists under the `jdbc` profile.)

No password encoding, event publishing, email/notification, or audit logging occurs anywhere in this flow.

## 4. Custom validators, exception handler, lifecycle callbacks

### Custom @Telephone validator
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/validation/Telephone.java` — constraint annotation (lines 15-22), `@Constraint(validatedBy = TelephoneValidator.class)`, default message "Telephone must be a valid E.164 number (+ and 8 to 15 digits)".
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/validation/TelephoneValidator.java` (lines 6-12) — valid iff `TelephoneNormalizer.toE164(telephone) != null`.
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/validation/TelephoneNormalizer.java` (lines 32-48) — strips spaces/dashes/parens; if it starts with `+` keeps the country code, otherwise assumes Australian `+61` and drops a single leading `0`; requires 8-15 digits after `+`, else returns null.

### Exception handler (@ControllerAdvice)
File: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/advice/ExceptionControllerAdvice.java`, `@ControllerAdvice` (line 49). Relevant handlers:
- `handleMethodArgumentNotValidException` (lines 133-169) — catches Bean Validation failures from `@Valid` on the DTO and returns 400 Bad Request as a `ProblemDetail`, populating an `errors` list of invalid field names and `schemaValidationErrors` messages formatted `Field '<field>' <message> (rejected value: <value>)`.
- `handleDataIntegrityViolationException` (lines 113-124) — DB constraint violations → 404 Not Found ProblemDetail.
- `handleAccessDeniedException` (lines 84-87) — re-throws so Spring Security handles 403/entry point.
- `handleGeneralException` (lines 96-103) — catch-all → 500.

Note: the 409 CONFLICT for the telephone / household duplicate checks is returned directly by the controller (not via this advice).

### Entity lifecycle callback (@PrePersist)
File: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java`
```java
119  @PrePersist
120  private void defaultRegistrationDate() {
121      if (this.registrationDate == null) {
122          this.registrationDate = LocalDate.now();
123      }
124  }
```
On first persist, defaults `registrationDate` to the server's current date (2026-09-17 at runtime) when the client omitted it. This is the only JPA lifecycle callback; there are no `@EntityListeners`, `@PostPersist`, or Spring `@EventListener`/ApplicationEvent listeners in the codebase.

Also on the entity (relevant side-effect): `setEmail` (Owner.java lines 95-97) lower-cases the email whenever it is set, so email is persisted in canonical lower-case. Bean-Validation constraints on the persisted entity: `Owner.address/city/telephone` are `@NotEmpty`, `telephone` also `@Pattern(regexp="^\\+[0-9]{8,15}$")` (lines 38-49); `Person.firstName/lastName` are `@NotEmpty` (`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Person.java`, lines 31-37).

Here is every validation and side-effect applied when creating an owner via **POST /api/owners**, in the order it actually happens.

## 1. Security pre-check
- `@PreAuthorize("hasRole(@roles.OWNER_ADMIN)")` — caller must hold the `OWNER_ADMIN` role, else 403. (`OwnerRestControllerV1.java:99`)

## 2. Bean Validation on the request body (`@Valid OwnerFieldsDto`)
Runs before the controller body; failures → **400 Bad Request** as a `ProblemDetail` (`ExceptionControllerAdvice.handleMethodArgumentNotValidException`). Per field:
- **firstName** — `@NotBlank`, `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..30)`, `@Pattern` `^[\p{L}]+([ '-][\p{L}]+){0,2}$` (letters, up to two separators)
- **lastName** — `@NotBlank`, `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..30)`, `@Pattern` `^[\p{L}]+([ '-][\p{L}]+){0,2}\.?$` (like firstName, trailing dot allowed)
- **address** — `@NotBlank`, `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..255)`
- **city** — `@NotBlank`, `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..80)`
- **telephone** — `@NotBlank`, `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..20)`, and custom `@Telephone` — valid only if `TelephoneNormalizer.toE164()` returns non-null (E.164: `+` and 8–15 digits; bare numbers assumed Australian `+61`)
- **email** — optional; if present `@Email` and `@Size(1..255)`
- **registrationDate** — optional `LocalDate`, no presence constraint
- **sharesHousehold** — `Boolean`, no constraints (write-only flag, never persisted)

## 3. DTO → entity mapping (`ownerMapper.toOwner`)
- `id` and `pets` ignored
- **telephone normalized to E.164** via `TelephoneNormalizer.toE164` (so all later checks use the normalized form)
- `email` passes through `Owner.setEmail`, which **lower-cases** it
- `sharesHousehold` has no entity field, so it is dropped after this point

## 4. Telephone uniqueness check (controller)
- `clinicService.existsOwnerByTelephone(owner.getTelephone())` — if an owner with the same (normalized) telephone exists → **409 Conflict**. (`OwnerRestControllerV1.java:104`)

## 5. Household uniqueness check (controller)
- **Skipped when `sharesHousehold == true`.** Otherwise `clinicService.existsOwnerInHousehold(lastName, address)`: finds owners with the same last name (case-insensitive) and matches on a canonicalized address (trim, collapse whitespace, lower-case). Match → **409 Conflict**. (`OwnerRestControllerV1.java:107-110`)

## 6. `clinicService.saveOwner(owner)` (transactional)
- If the owner is new and has no customer code, **generate a customer code**: `customerCodeGenerator.generate(lastName, ownerRepository.count() + 1)` → `<first-3-letters-upper>-<4-digit-seq>` (e.g. `SMI-0007`). Note this issues a `count()` DB query to drive the sequence number.
- **Persist** via `ownerRepository.save(owner)` (`em.persist` for new).

## 7. JPA `@PrePersist` lifecycle callback (`Owner.defaultRegistrationDate`)
- On first persist, if `registrationDate` is null, **default it to `LocalDate.now()`** (server date). (`Owner.java:119`)

## 8. Response construction
- Map saved entity → `OwnerDto` (`toOwnerDto`), which adds computed **`displayName`** (`"LastName, FirstName"`) and **`initials`** (e.g. `"G.F."`).
- Set **`Location` header** to `/api/owners/{id}`.
- Return **201 Created** with the DTO body.

---

**Notably absent** from this flow: no password encoding, no event publishing, no email/notification sending, and no audit logging. The only DB-level failure path is `DataIntegrityViolationException` → 404 via the advice; the two duplicate checks return 409 directly from the controller rather than through the exception handler.
